note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Static, isolated data selection motivates DWM, a bi-level-optimized data weighting model that improves pre-training and transfers

nodes.name: Selection ignores training dynamics
nodes.description: Existing LLM data selection methods mostly select data before training, ignoring the model's dynamic data preference during training.

nodes.name: Samples used indiscriminately
nodes.description: Existing methods select samples separately and use them indiscriminately within a batch, ignoring joint effects between samples that jointly determine the model update direction.

nodes.name: DWM weights data within batch
nodes.description: A plug-and-play Data Weighting Model (DWM) assigns weights to selected samples within each batch during LLM training to achieve dynamic data utilization.

nodes.name: Training loss is a bad upper objective
nodes.description: Updating the weighting model with the pre-training loss is sub-optimal because it can set weights of all or easily-predicted data to zero to minimize the loss.

nodes.name: Bi-level optimization of DWM
nodes.description: The weighting model is optimized at the upper level by maximizing validation performance of the LLM that is trained at the lower level on DWM-weighted data, using the chain rule.

nodes.name: Multi-stage alternating training
nodes.description: Training is split into stages and the DWM is re-learned at different stages by alternating iteration, to capture the model's shifting data preference.

nodes.name: DWM improves random-data pretraining
nodes.description: A 370M model pre-trained from scratch on randomly selected SlimPajama data performs better with DWM than without, in zero-shot and two-shot evaluation, with larger gains in later training stages.

nodes.name: Gains mainly in few-shot ability
nodes.description: DWM primarily improves few-shot performance rather than zero-shot, which the authors attribute to using LAMBADA as the validation set.

nodes.name: DWM transfers to other selectors and 1.3B
nodes.description: The DWM trained on 370M with random data transfers to DSIR- and QuRating-selected data and to a 1.3B Llama2-style model, giving consistent improvements.

nodes.name: Preferences shift during training
nodes.description: After stage 1 the DWM favors data scoring well on writing style, expertise, facts and education, but in later stages it prefers less well-written and more expertise-requiring data.

nodes.name: Static weighting models underperform
nodes.description: Fixed weighting models from the first stage (w1) or a late stage (w4) perform worse than the dynamically re-learned DWM, because early weights are too even and late weights bias toward high-quality data and reduce diversity.

nodes.name: More stages help modestly
nodes.description: Two-shot average accuracy of the 370M model is 45.1 (random), 45.3 (2 stages), 46.4 (DWM default), 46.5 (8 stages).

nodes.name: LAMBADA validation beats i.i.d. validation
nodes.description: Using LAMBADA as the validation task for the weighting model is more effective than an i.i.d. held-out SlimPajama validation set.

structural_reasoning: Motivation (static, indiscriminate data use) leads to the DWM and its bi-level multi-stage training, then to effectiveness, transfer, preference analysis and ablations.
